results.title: Kakao Q3 net profit down 7.9% to $132.7 mil.
results.content: South Korean internet tech giant Kakao on Thursday reported its third-quarter net income of 177.7 billion won ($132.7 million), down 7.9 percent from a year earlier. The company that operates KakaoTalk, the country's dominant messaging app, said in a regulatory filing that operating profit for the July-September period rose 15.5 percent on-year to 240.3 billion won. Sales remained unchanged at 2.08 trillion won. The earnings fell short of market expectations. The average estimate of net profit by analysts stood at 205.6 billion won, according to a survey by Yonhap Infomax, the financial data firm of Yonhap News Agency.

results.title: S. Korea posts record high current account surplus of over $60 bil. in Sept. on chip supercycle
results.content: South Korea posted an all-time high current account surplus of over $60 billion won in September on strong exports of semiconductors, central bank data showed Thursday. The current account surplus totaled $61.46 billion in September, up from $46.11 billion the previous month, according to the data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). It marked the largest monthly current account surplus ever, renewing the previous record of $49.73 billion set in June. Compared with the same month a year earlier, the figure surged from $14.22 billion. For the first nine months of the year, the current account surplus totaled a cumulative $340.66 billion, trebling from $83.89 billion recorded over the same period last year. results.title: N. Korea says it test-fired new air defense missile system
results.content: North Korea said Thursday it test-fired a newly designed air defense missile system the previous day to confirm its technical capabilities. The Missile Administration conducted the test, overseen by Kim Jong-sik, a member of the Central Military Commission, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported. "The test-fire proved the technical specifications and reliability of the new material and intelligent multiple guided mode of the projectile, target identification and tracking capability of the air-defence missile system and its detection information processing device," it said. In addition, a firepower subunit of the long-range strategic cruise missile unit in the eastern area staged a strike drill on the same day, using a long-range strategic cruise missile against a virtual airport target, according to the report. results.title: UNESCO likely to list traditional Korean paper 'hanji' as cultural heritage
results.content: The knowledge and skills associated with the production of "hanji," or traditional Korean paper, are likely to be added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage. UNESCO said Thursday its deliberative body has categorized "traditional knowledge and skills associated with the production of hanji, traditional Korean paper, and related cultural practices in the Republic of Korea" as recommended for inscription. The Republic of Korea is South Korea's official name. The tradition of hanji, paper made from the bark of mulberry trees, runs for about a thousand years and the meticulous handcrafting skills of hanji masters have been passed down through generations. The traditional paper has evolved over time, with hanji not only used for writing but also as a material for eco-friendly building, household products and artistic works. results.title: [ROUNDTABLE] Korea needs AI-ready ontology, should not end with developing models
results.content: Korea needs to diversify its current artificial intelligence (AI) strategy which is largely confined to developing advanced models, and expand its efforts to build AI-ready knowledge systems, infrastructure and a regulatory environment that supports practical applications, experts said during The Korea Times roundtable, “Beyond US-China AI race: Korea's strategic edge.” The participants called for greater efforts to build ontologies — structured knowledge systems that organize vast amounts of government data, institutional knowledge and the relationships between them into forms AI systems can understand and use. results.title: Democratic Congress could complicate S. Korea's nuclear sub plans, Trump-Kim summit: experts
results.content: WASHINGTON — Democratic control of the U.S. Congress could make it harder for South Korea to acquire nuclear-powered submarines and limit President Donald Trump's ability to reach a deal with North Korea, even as he may seek another summit with leader Kim Jong-un, according to experts Wednesday. The assessments came after the Democratic Party scored a landslide victory in Tuesday's midterm elections, with the party poised to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major political blow to Trump. Andrew Yeo, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, said Democrats could be more reluctant than Republicans to support South Korea's efforts to acquire nuclear-powered submarines because of concerns about the spread of nuclear technology. results.title: Korean celebrities reveal painful school bullying experiences
results.content: Korean television personality Lee Hye-sung has opened up about her painful experience of being bullied during her school years, drawing renewed attention to similar revelations by celebrities including actor Park Seo-joon, singer Sung Si-kyung and travel YouTuber KwakTube. On Friday, Lee discussed the bestselling self-help book "The Courage to Be Disliked" on her YouTube channel, Lee Hye-sung's 1% Book Club, offering advice to people struggling with school bullying and social exclusion. "If you think school is the only community where you belong, it can be incredibly painful when you're bullied or can't make friends," Lee said. "I've been through it myself."
